headline: Sox Drop Another To Twins As Fenway Bats Go Cold
morning_brew: Fenway Park saw another tough one on Saturday as the Red Sox dropped their second straight to the Twins in a four to two defeat. Jovani Moran got the start but lasted only one inning, giving up two runs on three hits before the bullpen had to take over. Brayan Bello did some heavy lifting by eating five innings of relief and giving up zero earned runs, but the damage was already done. Five hits from the Sox lineup is just not going to get the job done when you are trying to climb out of a hole.

Are you kiddin' me with this? We had some momentum last week, and now we are staring at a twenty-two and twenty-nine record after back-to-back losses at home. Willson Contreras had a decent night at the plate with two hits, but the rest of the order could not string anything together against Taj Bradley. It is absolutely brutal to watch this offense go cold right when the pitching staff actually holds an opponent to four runs. If this team wants to crawl back toward five hundred, they need to find some consistency before this homestand gets away from them.

Football season is still months away, but Patriots wide receiver Kyle Williams is already making headlines with his offseason training adjustments. Reports out of Foxborough say he is changing up his routine to take his game to the next level for his second season. With the offensive struggles this franchise has endured lately, any sign of dedication from the young receiving corps is a massive positive. Let us hope these offseason adjustments translate to some actual production on the field when camp opens up.

news_digest.headline: Patriots WR Kyle Williams making key offseason changes
news_digest.dans_take: Love seeing the kid put in the work early to help Drake Maye next season.
